datasets.label: Hubble · optical
datasets.title: The Homunculus, ultraviolet to visible
datasets.description: ESA/Hubble's picture of the Homunculus Nebula, at 220, 250, 330, 550 and 660 nm: dust lit by the star Eta Carinae inside it. It lies on the surface Steffen et al. (2014) made from spectra of the whole nebula: two hollow lobes, their pole 41° from the sight line (Smith 2006), the south-east one tipped toward the Sun. The picture is on the side of each lobe that faces the Sun; the other sides, which no one has photographed, repeat it. Around the lobes, a gas cloud this repository derived, neither observed in 3D nor published: each knot of the outer ejecta placed in depth from its motion across the sky (Hubble) and its speed along the sight line (MUSE), its brightness and color from Hubble's [N II] images, and the far side mirrored from the near one.
datasets.summary: Hubble's picture on the published 3D lobes, inside a gas cloud derived here from Hubble and MUSE motions and images.

inputEvidence.evidence: The gas cloud drawn around the lobes in this dataset: source/cloud-points.json, baked into billboards by packages/bake/cli/prepare-cloud-points.mts.

datasets.label: Outer shell · model
datasets.title: The outer shell of the 1840s ejecta
datasets.description: the 1840s ejecta outside the Homunculus as one bent tube, after the SHAPE model of Mehner et al. (2016), its wall refitted here to MUSE H-beta emission. A model, not an observation.
datasets.summary: The 1840s ejecta's outer shell, a bent cylinder after Mehner et al. (2016), refitted to MUSE spectra.

datasets.label: Motions · measured
datasets.title: How the outer ejecta move
datasets.description: each knot of the outer ejecta and where it moves in the next century: its motion across the sky measured on Hubble images, its speed along the sight line from MUSE spectra.
datasets.summary: Each knot's next century: sky motion from Hubble images, line-of-sight speed from MUSE. Blue approaches.
